description: Versioned index of the RBI corpus. Every field under `applicability` is a hard filter applied against the uploaded document's own metadata BEFORE reranking, so a passage that does not govern this loan never reaches the model. An empty array means 'unrestricted on this axis'.

field_notes.applicability.effective_from: Date the obligations actually bind a loan. Deliberately distinct from issued_on: several of these circulars were issued months before they took effect, and a loan sanctioned in the gap is not governed by them.
field_notes.applicability.effective_to: null means still in force as far as this corpus knows.
field_notes.verified_from_pdf: true means the reference number, date and addressees below were read out of the PDF text, not assumed from the filename.
field_notes.source_url: Fetched and confirmed to match this PDF's own reference number, circular number and date. source_url_verified records that check; a citation must never link somewhere it was merely assumed to point.

documents.title: Master Circular - Fair Practices Code
topics: loan application processing
disbursement and changes in terms and conditions
loan appraisal and terms
excessive interest
repossession of vehicles
NBFC-MFI disclosures in loan agreement / loan card
non-coercive recovery
lending against gold jewellery
documents.notes: Consolidates instructions as at June 30, 2012 and supersedes CC No.232 dated July 01, 2011. NBFC-specific: it does NOT bind banks. RECOMMENDED REPLACEMENT: the NBFC Fair Practices Code has since been restated in later Master Directions, so grounding a compliance claim in this 2012 text risks citing a rule that has moved. Kept in the corpus for coverage, but any answer resting solely on it should be treated as weaker evidence than the 2023-2025 circulars.
documents.source_url_status: Not resolved. This 2012 Master Circular is superseded and no longer listed in RBI's current master-circular index; the pages that surface under this title today are the 2011-12 predecessor it replaced (RBI/2011-12/26) and the later 2015-16 edition (RBI/2015-16/16). No URL is recorded rather than one that is close but wrong. See notes: this document should be replaced in the corpus.

documents.title: Fair Lending Practice - Penal Charges in Loan Accounts
addressees: All Commercial Banks (including Small Finance Banks, Local Area Banks and Regional Rural Banks, excluding Payments Banks)
All India Financial Institutions (EXIM Bank, NABARD, NHB, SIDBI and NaBFID)
topics: penal charges must not be levied as penal interest
no capitalisation of penal charges
board approved policy on penal charges
penal charges must be reasonable and non-discriminatory
individual non-business borrowers not to be charged more than non-individuals
disclosure of penal charges in loan agreement and KFS
communication of penal charges to borrower
documents.notes: Issued 2023-08-18. The circular itself said 'These instructions shall come into effect from January 1, 2024', but DoR.MCS.REC.61/01.01.001/2023-24 dated 2023-12-29 extended that by three months. effective_from is therefore 2024-04-01, the date fresh loans actually became subject to it; for existing loans the switchover ran to the next review/renewal on or after 2024-04-01 and no later than 2024-06-30. Taking the date printed in the circular at face value would have had FinX judge a loan against rules that were not yet in force.

documents.notes: PDF is the version 'Updated as on October 1, 2025'. Compliance deadline in the text: 'REs shall ensure that the above instructions are extended to the existing as well as new loans suitably by December 31, 2023', which is why effective_from is 2023-12-31 rather than the issue date. 'Personal loans' follows the RBI retail definition, hence the loan_types list covering housing, vehicle and education alongside consumer credit. source_url is the one self-referential rbi.org.in link embedded in the PDF.

documents.source_capture: rbidocs.rbi.org.in serves its PDFs behind a bot-protection challenge, so this file was rendered locally from the verbatim text of the notification page at source_url rather than downloaded as RBI's own PDF. The wording is the circular's; the typesetting is not. Replace it with the official PDF when one can be fetched by hand.
documents.notes: Short and entirely operative: it moves the penal-charges compliance date. Replaced the file previously carrying this name, which was in fact the UCB Master Circular on Management of Advances (RBI/2025-26/18) -- 244 chunks of co-operative-bank material that governs no NBFC or bank loan.

documents.notes: Binding for all new retail and MSME term loans sanctioned on or after 2024-10-01, including fresh loans to existing customers, which is the effective_from used here rather than the 2024-04-15 issue date. This circular is the regulatory basis for the KFS-vs-agreement audit in app/risk/kfs_diff.py.

documents.title: Reserve Bank of India (Pre-payment Charges on Loans) Directions, 2025
topics: no pre-payment charges on floating rate loans to individuals for non-business purposes
pre-payment charges for business loans to individuals and MSEs by lender tier
no minimum lock-in period
pre-payment permitted irrespective of source of funds
cash credit and overdraft facilities
disclosure of pre-payment charges in the Key Facts Statement
documents.notes: The sharpest effective-date case in this corpus: 'These Directions shall be applicable to all loans and advances sanctioned or renewed on or after January 1, 2026.' A loan sanctioned before that date is not governed by it, so the as_of filter must exclude these passages for older agreements even though they are the most semantically similar match for any prepayment question. Obligations vary by lender tier (NBFC-UL vs NBFC-ML, UCB Tier 3 vs Tier 4) and by whether the purpose is business, which the clause-level chunks must preserve.

repeals.note: Repealed only from 2026-01-01, and the Directions add that the repealed circulars 'shall be deemed to have been in force during the relevant periods, prior to the coming into effect of these instructions'. So a loan sanctioned before 2026-01-01 is still governed by the older foreclosure circulars, not by these Directions. None of the repealed circulars are in this corpus, so FinX cannot answer a prepayment question about a pre-2026 loan from primary sources and should say so rather than reaching for the 2025 Directions.
